chats.answer:
For running Paperless-ngx as a long-term scanned document archive, I'd recommend a 2-bay or 4-bay Intel-based NAS with Docker support, at least 8 GB RAM, and SSD storage for the application and database.

Paperless-ngx is relatively lightweight, but its OCR processing, document indexing, and optional AI features can benefit from a faster CPU.

My priorities would be:

Reliable Docker support — Paperless-ngx runs well using Docker Compose.

Intel x86-64 CPU — Broad compatibility and good OCR performance.

8–16 GB RAM — 8 GB is plenty for a personal archive; 16 GB offers more headroom.

SSD for PostgreSQL and application data — Improves responsiveness and indexing.

Snapshot and backup support — Particularly important for irreplaceable scanned documents.

You don't need a powerful NAS just to store PDFs. The bigger consideration is how quickly it can process newly scanned documents and how reliably it preserves them over many years.

For running Paperless-ngx as a long-term scanned document archive, I'd prioritize a NAS with reliable Docker support, SSD storage for the application, sufficient RAM for OCR, and a good backup system.

You don't need a particularly powerful NAS for Paperless-ngx. But you do want one that can run reliably for years, handle OCR processing without slowing down, and protect important documents.

My top choices are Synology Plus-series NAS devices for simplicity, or an Intel-based NAS running TrueNAS or Unraid for flexibility.

A typical scanned PDF archive doesn't need much disk space. Even tens of thousands of documents can fit comfortably on a few terabytes, depending on scan quality.

The main performance consideration is OCR and document ingestion, especially if you're importing a large existing collection of scanned PDFs.
